name: What permits are required for a second-story addition in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Which permits are typically needed for a second-story addition in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood, and are there separate trade permits?
mainEntity.text: Which permits are typically needed for a second-story addition in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, or North Hollywood, and are there separate trade permits?

acceptedAnswer.text: A second-story addition almost always needs more than one permit. The core permit is the building permit, but the project may also require separate electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits because the new floor affects all major systems in the home. Structural plans and engineering calculations are typically part of the permit package, and the city may also require zoning review, plan check approval, and sometimes additional review for overlays, historic properties, or special districts. In some cases, homeowners also need permit coordination for demolition, grading, tree protection, or utility upgrades. The exact combination depends on the jurisdiction and the scope of work. A project in Los Angeles may follow different administrative steps than one in Pasadena or Glendale, so homeowners should confirm requirements early rather than assuming a standard addition package will be enough. The safest approach is to assemble the full permit path before construction begins so the project does not stall after demolition or framing has already started.
acceptedAnswer.description: A second-story addition usually needs a building permit plus separate permits for structural-related work and building trades such as electrical, plumbing, and mechanical systems. Depending on the city and property, zoning review, plan check approval, and additional approvals for special districts may also be required.
